event.title: 2026 Belle Meade Society Fall Dinner
event.description:
The Greensboro History Museum’s Belle Meade Society will have its annual Fall Dinner at the museum on Monday, October 5, 2026. The evening starts at 5:30 pm and includes dinner, wine and a presentation by Kevin von der Lippe.

Drawing from the research conducted for the book Greensboro Depot, local railroad enthusiast von der Lippe will discuss how photographs, newspapers, maps, railroad records, and materials from private collections were assembled to document the history of one of Greensboro’s best-known landmarks. The presentation will feature images from the book as well as several photographs that did not appear in the final publication, providing a behind-the-scenes look at the sources and methods used to preserve and share local history.

$45 per person. Please RSVP by Friday, September 25.

Purchase Your Tickets Online

It isn’t too late to become a Belle Meade member, by upgrading your current membership or joining anew. We hope to see you!

event.title: Richard Kurin, History by a Hair: Thomas Jefferson, Sally Hemings & Solving a 200-Year-Old Mystery
event.description:
The Smithsonian Institution’s Distinguished Scholar and Ambassador-at-Large Richard Kurin discusses his new book.

History by a Hair is the definitive account of how a discarded strand of hair found in Thomas Jefferson’s Bible at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History led to a sweeping, multi-year genomic investigation, drawing on technological advances in DNA to finally resolve a 200-year national controversy.

Book signing to follow with copies available to purchase from Scuppernong Books.

Spaces are limited. Let us know you are attending. 

About the author
Richard Kurin is the Smithsonian Institution’s Distinguished Scholar and Ambassador-at-Large and previously served as Under Secretary overseeing all museums and scientific centers. An author of several popular books on American history and Fellow of the American Academy of Arts & Sciences, Kurin has led major national cultural initiatives and produced award-winning public history.

This event is part of the Greensboro History Museum’s America250 community programming. event.title: Revolutionary Road Trip: A Conversation with Darley Newman
event.description:
Travel expert Darley Newman chats with Museum Director Carol Ghiorsi Hart about her new book, Revolutionary Road Trip: Hidden Stories of America’s Founding Journey. The book follows the host of PBS’s Travels with Darley on a journey through American Revolution sites, including right here in Guilford County.

Seats are limited. Registration for this event is coming soon. Check back for more information.

About the author

Darley Newman is an award-winning host, producer, author, and travel expert recognized by Forbes for building a “PBS media empire.” She’s blended world-record feats with purposeful storytelling—from leaping off the world’s highest commercial bungee in Macao to riding horses across Botswana to interviewing civil rights witnesses and small business owners in rural United States. As the creator and host of Travels with Darley, Equitrekking, and Look Up with Darley, she combines travel, history, and narrative to uncover hidden gems across the United States and around the world. A trusted, authentic voice, her series and podcast reach dedicated fans on PBS, Amazon Prime, iHeart, and internationally in more than eighty-five nations. Darley has earned multiple Emmy Award nominations for hosting, writing, producing, and directing. She’s been honored with the North American Travel Journalist Award, Inspiring Woman Award, two Telly Awards, and induction into the Taste Awards Hall of Fame. Having filmed her series in destinations as close to home as New York City and Los Angeles and as far afield as Seoul, Uruguay, and Dubai, she inspires audiences to explore beyond their comfort zones. She is a graduate of The George Washington University.
